invariant: All gates proven effective must be proven to be fully transitioned to native source level before they are deprecated. Registration in handlers.ts is NOT activation — it makes a handler selectable and nothing more.

statuses.devolved: The native replacement is activated: handler_ref resolves, the descriptor ships in DEFAULT_HOOK_SET, and the seam dispatches it today.
statuses.pending_activation: The host hook is still registered and the transition is not finished. A named debt, not a pass: `reason` says what is missing.
statuses.retained: LEGIBLE ONLY FOR A ROW THAT IS NOT A LIVE REGISTRATION. The operator ruled zero retentions, so `gate:hook-devolution` rejects this status on any hook that is still registered. It exists here only to keep a record of something already unregistered.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30. THIS ROW WAS THE LAST PENDING ACTIVATION IN THE PROGRAMME, and its recorded reason said the blocker was THE TRIGGER, not the logic: the hook fired on the HOST session start, before the host first model action, while revoy2 native session_start fires only after `arbor task` admission. Both halves of that reason were acted on. THE LOGIC IS NOT PORTED, AND DELIBERATELY SO: `scripts/decision-queue.mjs` is 795 lines over 9 sources and 3 scripts/lib deps, and `gate:decision-queue` enforces the result. A TypeScript reimplementation would be a SECOND implementation of an invariant the gate already owns, and that drift is SILENT in the worst direction available — the interview would be owed, the injected queue would not mention it, and nothing anywhere would say so. So `inject.operator-decision-queue` SUBPROCESSES `bun scripts/decision-queue.mjs --json` (the same script `repo-session-lifecycle.ts` already subprocesses at the session close) and maps the JSON to a Tropism. Shelling out from a package is legitimate and precedented (cli.ts, native-tools/evidence-refresh.ts, repo-session-lifecycle.ts); the claim in git-write-guard.ts that gate:package-boundaries forbade it was FALSE — that gate reads import specifiers, never argv — and was corrected in 234dcf7b. The parity is asserted, not asserted-about: operator-decision-queue-tropism.test.ts derives the queue ONCE by subprocess and asserts the rendered rows against an independent filter over that same object, and separately pins the argv to ["--json", "--repo", <root>] against a stub script, so a divergence from the gate is not a thing the test could miss. WHAT THE HANDLER DOES NOT DO, stated because it is the guarantee being preserved: it READS and RENDERS. It has no write path — it cannot write decisions/interviews.jsonl, cannot record coverage, cannot edit a status or a waiver, and cannot answer for the operator. That was never the shell hook property either; it lives in LEGAL_TRANSITIONS (packages/arbor-governance/src/record/status.ts) plus a store that only PARSES the interview ledger, and a read-only handler cannot weaken either. THE TIMING CHANGED AND IS STATED, NOT PAPERED OVER. The honest native guarantee is: a revoy2-DRIVEN session cannot cross its first model action without the uncovered operator queue being surfaced. It is NOT the operator editor opening a terminal — revoy2 does not own that moment and this row does not claim to reproduce it. THE ADVISORY-IMPERATIVE LINT FORCED A WORDING CHANGE: the script opened `MANDATORY REVOY2 SESSION-START INTERVIEW`, which catalog.ts REFUSES for an ADVISORY tropism (must/shall/should/never/always/do-not at the first token). The ported body opens with a noun phrase and keeps the imperative on a later line, so the lint cannot reach it. THE THREE KINDS AND THE HAZARDS ARE THE SCRIPT S OWN, in its fixed order: proposed_record, operator_decision, operator_call, then a governance hazards section; waiver, vi_triage, completion_depth and discharge_obligation rows are deliberately EXCLUDED because they are owed work, not operator CHOICES, and a covered row is not owed. derived_from hashes exactly the rows the body is composed of, so 5.3 rule 2 suppresses a re-render when the queue has not moved — which is also this handler sharpest failure mode, since a queue that stopped being read does not lie, it disappears, and a session finding nothing here cannot tell that from a session with nothing owed. The script is deleted in this commit, with its .codex/hooks.json and scripts/host-controls.json registrations, its scripts/tests/ unit test (coverage moved to the native test), and its .hook-liveness/hook-manifest.json entry.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30. The blocker recorded here was 'NO PORTABLE INPUT' — a native veto handler was given only a bounded command string. That is no longer true: W3 (dce95df5) gave HookVetoToolInput `path`, `added_text` and `removed_text`, and `added_text` is exactly what this guard greps while `removed_text` is what makes its 'marker already present' discharge reachable at all. THE FIDELITY TRAP WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the bus truncates text to a 1024-byte head, and a 5,031-byte ROADMAP.md write reached the handler as 1,024 bytes with its **CLOSED** row invisible — a refusal the shell hook had made, silently converted to an allow. Fixed by a per-handler `text_bytes` on the registry entry (mirroring W7a's `timeout_ms`), set to 128 KiB because that is exactly what file.write/file.patch already bound `content`/`expected`/`replacement` at in the production composition (cli.ts `max_read_bytes: 128 * 1024`), so the bus never truncates a call the tool would have accepted. Measured against the real targets: decisions/README.md is 23,754 B and the largest of 167 ADRs is 26,589 B, both read whole; ROADMAP.md is 192,920 B, which EXCEEDS the bound and therefore cannot be whole-written at all, so it must be patched with a bounded `replacement` also read whole. A text AT the bound is refused as unread-in-full rather than assumed marker-free, so raising a bound later fails visibly instead of quietly un-guarding. Descriptor `claim-completeness-guard` ships in DEFAULT_HOOK_SET (hooks/catalog.ts) and `HookCatalog.fromDirectory` registers the source defaults in memory when `.arbor/hooks` is absent. Proven from real disk through wrapToolPort in packages/arbor-mcp/tests/hooks/file-write-guards.test.ts, the test that failed before this change.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30. The blocker recorded here was 'WRONG DENIAL SHAPE' — the script denies by `exit 0` plus a {"permissionDecision":"deny"} payload, and porting that as a veto was judged to invert the script's fail-OPEN intent. That reading was correct about the shape and wrong about the consequence. The shell convention is not a denial-by-exit-code convention: the script exits 0 on EVERY deliberate path including its refusals, and a `HookVetoDecision` returned directly does not invert anything — it carries the same decision over the same exit code. What the inversion argument DID correctly identify is a real defect, and the handler removes it: vi-readonly-guard.sh was the only one of the five host hooks that could exit NON-ZERO, and only accidentally, from three unguarded cat/jq calls under `set -euo pipefail` (:15, :18, :47) — a malformed payload turned a no-op into a hard failure carrying no decision. A handler has no exit code to get wrong, so that mode is gone by construction rather than by having found and fixed all three sites. Every fail-open is preserved deliberately: no `.visual-intelligence` directory, sentinel absent, sentinel STALE past VI_SENTINEL_STALE_SECONDS (default 14400, overridable by the same env var), and an unreadable path — with the stale case load-bearing, because a leaked sentinel is the EXPECTED failure of an interrupted run and would otherwise brick all editing in the repository. Containment resolves both sides before comparing, as `realpath -m` did, so `..` and a symlinked directory are caught. Descriptor `vi-readonly-guard` ships in DEFAULT_HOOK_SET (hooks/catalog.ts). Proven from real disk through wrapToolPort in packages/arbor-mcp/tests/hooks/file-write-guards.test.ts, the test that failed before this change.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30. The blocker recorded here was 'NO PORTABLE INPUT' — `tool_audit` observe events carry only a bounded summary/detail and the post-execution audit path has no path in it. That is still true of the AUDIT path, and the fix was NOT to widen it: `NativeToolAuditRecord` is content-free by design (native-tools/contracts.ts, 'raw paths, argv, and scope ids never leave the host'), and bus.ts forbids also wrapping a repository tool's `execute` because that fires tool_audit twice for one action. So the event is fired from the side that HAS the path — the tool-INPUT side, in wrapToolPort's preflight, where request.input.path is what the tool is about to act on. That required a new observe event (`tool_write`), because the audit path cannot carry one. PRE-FIRING IS THE HONEST COST: the script was PostToolUse and this fires before the call executes, so .dirty records paths a session ATTEMPTED, a superset of paths it changed. It costs no fidelity here because BOTH consumers (vi-freshness.sh's dirty_count, vi-graph-debt.sh's debt count) intersect .dirty with git status, so an attempt that then failed intersects nothing — and it fires only after the base port's own preflight admits the call, so a vetoed or refused write is not recorded at all. What .dirty uniquely adds over git status is unchanged: it remembers a path that was edited AND THEN COMMITTED, which git status cannot show. `HookObserveContext.detail` was NOT redacted before this change (only `summary` was); it now is, at HOOK_MAX_DETAIL_VALUE_BYTES = 1024 — the same bound native-tool-host already enforces on its own `path` field (stringField(value, 'path', 1, 1_024)), so the bus never truncates a path the tool would have accepted. A path sitting exactly AT the bound may be a head rather than the whole value, and the handler DROPS it: a truncated line in .dirty can never intersect git status, so it is drift that reports as permanent cleanliness. The redacted form is what lands on disk, so a path matching a secret shape (api_key=…, Bearer …) is recorded as [REDACTED] and will not intersect git status — a lost entry, never a wrong one, and that is the safe direction. DROPPED DELIBERATELY: the script's `.tool_input.notebook_path` fallback. There is no native equivalent — file.write and file.patch are the only path-carrying write tools and neither declares that field — and a fallback key no tool populates is a branch nothing can ever exercise. EVERY SKIP RULE PRESERVED: silent skip under .visual-intelligence/ (the graph's own output is not drift), silent skip outside the repository, and total inertness where .visual-intelligence/ does not exist, which is what makes global installation safe. Containment is tested on the RELATIVE form rather than by stripping a $cwd/ prefix as the script did, so a path escaping through `..` reads as outside instead of passing as repo-relative. Append-only, exactly once per path, never sorted, never deduped against deletes — the two readers count non-empty lines (vi-render.mjs:82) and vi-refresh.mjs:749 truncates, so the format is unchanged and both still behave. Descriptor `vi-dirty-tracker` ships in DEFAULT_HOOK_SET (hooks/catalog.ts), and `wrapToolPort` wraps when a `tool_write` observe hook is declared even when no veto hook is — otherwise the handler would be one no tool call can reach, the same registration-is-not-activation defect the ledger's own gate exists to catch. Proven from real disk through the real NativeRepositoryToolHost's file.write and file.patch in packages/arbor-mcp/tests/hooks/vi-dirty-tracker.test.ts, the test that failed before this change.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30 onto the turn_end OBSERVE event (HookBus.observeTurnEnd), which the previous W7b-1 commit built and left unclaimed. THE MODEL-FACING QUESTION WAS DECIDED AGAINST A NEW CHANNEL, and it is the substantive choice in this row. The script's whole product was prose printed to the model at Stop time. An observe handler's product is a bounded ledger note (HookObserveOutcome has no tropism and no other text field), and the alternative was available: contracts.ts's HOOK_INJECT_EVENTS would have had to gain turn_end, because HookCatalog refuses an inject descriptor on any event but a lifecycle one. That was rejected on contracts.ts's own stated reason — a tropism is derived from a moment in a session's life, so the six lifecycle events are already exactly the right moments, and adding an inject-only event makes HOOK_ALL_EVENTS stop being the set of names the bus dispatches. A second injection channel minted so a reminder could reach the model is the 'changes nothing for this entry point' trap in new dress. The information is not lost to the model: inject.vi-freshness (descriptor session-graph-freshness) reports the same .dirty ∩ git status intersection at SessionStart and its DIVERGED rung names the uncommitted path count. What this handler adds is the UNSCOPED count, refreshed every turn instead of once a session. THE INTERSECTION IS THE SHARED HELPER, NOT A SECOND COPY: dirtyIntersection(git, root, []) from vi-freshness-tropism.ts, with an EMPTY scope, because the script's git status --porcelain was unscoped and deliberately so — a debt report that hid docs/ edits would under-report the debt it exists to show, and the under-count reads as 'the graph is clean'. The sibling's packages/+decisions/ scope is a DIFFERENT question (did the graphed domain drift), and the test asserts the contrast directly: docs/readme.md counts here and does not count there. Line shapes are the script's exactly, and paths touched-then-committed are still not debt. derived_from IS A HASH OF THE INTERSECTED PATH SET, and this required a small bus change to be expressible at all: HookObserveOutcome gained an optional derived_from and fireObserve now records it on the row (observeDerivedFrom drops a malformed declaration whole rather than filtering it, so a row can never carry [null] or ['']). It is LEDGER-ONLY and is NOT deduped — §5.3 rule 2's dedupe belongs to the inject lane, and the observe lane records every firing. It exists because a native handler is invisible to scripts/hook-liveness-gate.mjs, which reads stdout from shell scripts, and because this repository has a recorded ~42-session instance of a hook emitting a confident fixed verdict after it stopped measuring (ADR-032). On the inject lane the native form of that failure is SILENCE — a derivation that stops moving is deduped away; on this lane it is a derivation that stops moving, which is at least visible in a diff of two rows. PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: two assertions fail when the hash input is forced to a constant (verified by running it), two identical firings must carry an IDENTICAL derivation and an identical note, and a firing with no debt carries NO derivation at all rather than an invented one. ONE DECLARED ADAPTATION. The observe lane slices a note to HOOK_MAX_NOTE_BYTES (512) as a HEAD slice, so the script's head-5 sample of long paths would silently amputate the remedy — the one actionable line in the message. Sample rows are therefore shed from the end until the whole message fits, and what is no longer shown is counted in the '... and N more' row, which is what that row is for. The header's count is never reduced. FIVE SILENCES, the script's own: no .dirty (which is also what makes global installation safe outside a repository that uses the skill), an empty worktree listing, an empty intersection, a zero count, and a .dirty with no live path in it. Silence is void, not an empty note, so a healthy turn costs one ledger row carrying the event summary. THE SHAPE DECISION THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE STATED: the script printed PLAIN TEXT on stdout with no hookSpecificOutput envelope, and the native handler keeps that shape — one line, up to five four-space sample rows, the hidden-count row, the remedy — rather than adopting a JSON envelope, because the note is a human- and ledger-readable message and a descriptor-shaped wrapper would add a field nothing reads. Descriptor `vi-graph-debt` ships in DEFAULT_HOOK_SET (hooks/catalog.ts) bound to the turn_end event, and the registry entry declares timeout_ms: 2000 for the same reason inject.vi-freshness does — it spawns git, the bus's 50ms default is sized for a pure in-process predicate, and crossing it would drop the note; an overrun is still visible as error=hook_timeout_exceeded. The script is deleted in this commit, and with it its .claude/settings.json and scripts/host-controls.json registrations, its scripts/vi-install-hooks.mjs HOOKS row, and its .hook-liveness/hook-manifest.json declaration. The liveness row was the one place the dead script's WHY was recorded, and it is preserved here: the hook that actually rotted is the reason this replacement's derivation is tested to move. STILL OPEN and NOT claimed here: gate-stop.sh and stop-guard.mjs are separate rows and this commit touches neither.

DEVOLVED 2026-09-30. The blocker recorded here was 'A VERDICT LADDER, NOT A BOOLEAN — a native observe handler's return type has no admission or severity field, so there is nowhere to put a ladder.' The ladder went in as an INJECT tropism rather than an observe note, because a Tropism is the plane's typed multi-valued channel and `null` is its own verdict: returning null IS the script's `quiet`, so all five rungs and both silencers survive as real returns rather than as prose in a note nobody can act on. All five rungs reproduce in the script's order, first match wins: UNCOMMITTED-BASIS (tree_state=dirty), CURRENT, DIVERGED (uncommitted AND behind, both facts always reported), DIVERGED (uncommitted alone), STALE. Then the script's two silencers, after the ladder rather than inside it: CURRENT injects nothing, and a STALE whose commits missed packages/+decisions/ injects nothing, because a stale graph describing untouched code is still accurate. A third silence is the script's own `quiet` before it has a manifest to read, which is also what keeps the handler inert in a clone that does not use the skill.
